text.p: Construction firm Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had maintained uncompleted work at hand at A$3.3 billion as at September 30, 1996 and that the outlook remained positive.

"New work won in Australia and Asia during the first quarter of the 1996/97 financial year had kept work levels steady at the record level achieved at the end of the previous period," Leighton chief executive Wal King said in a statement.
"Overall, the outlook remains very positive," he said.
Leighton said revenue for the first quarter was in line with expectations and that it had a mix of new projects spanning its core construction and mining markets.
"A highlight was the recent award to Thiess Contractors of a A$200 million joint venture contract for a telecommunicaitons project in Central Java in Indonesia," King said.
"Theiss has established a broad base of construction and mining work in Indonesia and this contract boosts an already strong workload in that country," he said.
Leighton Asia had been successful in securing work, particularly in newer markets like Malaysia and the Philippines.
"Whilst the Australian economy remains patchy, there continues to be good prospects in a number of markets where our operations have a strong presence," King said.
"Overal the outlook remains very positive," he said.
Leighton, 44.9 percent owned by German construction group Hochtief Ag, reported a net profit of A$70.21 million for the year to June 30, up from A$51.23 million in 1994/95.
